# Review of beowulf-fitt-43 (lines 3137-3182)

Reviewer: adversarial, two passes. Files edited in place by script: units.json (never `t`, `ln`, `v`) and gloss.json. Sources checked: packet.md (text, italics, apparatus), source/beowulf-klaeber1922.json (cross-references 352, 1122, 1408, 2802 ff., 2999 ff., 3069 ff., 3094 ff.), published parts (fitt-01, 04, 05, 17, 35, 42 and a grep of every root beowulf-fitt-*.json for hlāford, þēoden, wīgend, byrne, sigle, mǣnan, mondryhten, bānhūs, bēna).

Counts. Pass 1 (units.json): 27 changes, high 1, medium 10, low 16. Pass 2 (units.json): 2 changes, high 0, medium 0, low 2. Gloss (gloss.json): 11 entries changed, high 0, medium 2, low 9.

## Pass 1 — units.json

Changes (line · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

1. 3137 · l · medium · "as he had been a petitioner" renders a pluperfect for `wæs` (preterite). · "as he was a petitioner" (matches the house l of `swā þū bēna eart`, fitt-05).
2. 3137 · n · medium · Said "Thorkelin and others" read `behēngon`; the apparatus gives Tr., Holt.1, Sed. (Trautmann, Holthausen first edition, Sedgefield); Thk. is not cited there. · Attribution corrected.
3. 3137 · n · low · "as at 350": the phrase `swā þū bēna eart` is line 352 (350 is the unit start). · "352".
4. 3137 · n · low · Closing sentence pointed ahead to the dot at 3165 ("explained there") in a unit with no dot; the real explanation was missing at 3165 (see 20). · Sentence removed.
5. 3141 · n · low · "loaf-guardian, the man who keeps bread for his household" asserts a social claim and departs from fitt-04's "loaf-keeper". · "generally derived from hlāf-weard, loaf-keeper, though the poem itself gives no sign of that origin". The etymology is kept only hedged (usual, public-domain lexical derivation).
6. 3144 · i · low · "the wind had dropped" shifts tense (gelæg is a plain preterite, l "lay down"). · "the wind lay still".
7. 3144 · n · low · `ðā bānhūs`: the demonstrative was not accounted for (ðā is the plural article or the adverb; hūs is identical in sg. and pl.). · Sentence added; l keeps "the bone-house".
8. 3148 · i · low · "mourned their grief" is tautological and does not render `mōdceare` as an object well. · "bewailed their sorrow".
9. 3150 · l, n · low · l "(for Beowulf)" for `(æfter Bīowulfe)`, and the note never mentioned the phrase. · l "(after Beowulf)"; note sentence added (Bugge's restoration; "in mourning for Beowulf").
10. 3150 · l/i/n · medium · `(wīgen)des egesan`: l "terror" (sg.), i "an enemy's terrors" (pl., and "enemy" is not in the text), note "terrors"; glossary entry for `egesan` is sg. · All three now singular and "a warrior's terror"; note says `egesan` can be sg. or pl.
11. 3150 · n · low · `hȳ[n]ðo` called "humiliations" (pl.) while l and i are singular. · Note now "humiliation (the form may be read as singular or plural)".
12. 3150 · n · medium · "It is the fear of a people whose king is dead and who face the Swedes ..." stated as fact; the lines (Bugge's restoration) name no enemy and no people. · Recast as the reviewer's/drafter's inference ("I read it as ..."), flagged as inference and as Bugge's restoration.
13. 3156 · i · medium · "the wisest men": `foresnotre` is positive (fore- intensive), and the note and l say "very wise". · "very wise men".
14. 3156 · n · low · "the e of g(e)sȳne is in round brackets as a letter in doubt": round brackets mean lost letters (conventions). · "lost or doubtful in the manuscript".
15. 3156 · n · low · lemma `beweorcan` vs the glossary's `bewyrcan`. · Made `bewyrcan`.
16. 3163 · i · medium · "bold, grim-minded men": `bold` has no source in `nīðhēdịge` (nīð + -hēdig) and sounds remembered. · "grim-minded men".
17. 3163 · n · medium · `hyrsta` called accusative plural; it is the genitive plural (partitive after `eall swylce`; the nom./acc. pl. of hyrst is hyrste), and gloss.json already had genitive. · Corrected, literal gloss added.
18. 3163 · n · low · `bēg`: apparatus gives Tho. `bēag[as]` but Tr., Holt. `bēg[as]`; the note merged them. · Both readings stated.
19. 3163 · n · medium · "the Geats who carried the hoard out ... Wiglaf first": "Wiglaf first" is not in the line or in Klaeber's apparatus; the identification of the men is a guess. · "Wiglaf first" struck; marked "a guess; the line does not name them".
20. 3163 · n · medium · The dot under the vowel was not explained in this part (conventions: explain it the first time a part meets one); the note said "first explained in the third part", which is also not where the standing statement is (fitt-01/02 sources carry it). · One-sentence explanation written here.
21. 3166 · n · low · lemma `eld` vs the glossary's `ylde`. · Made `ylde`.
22. 3169 · n · high · Jordanes parallel stated wrongly: "a ride in a ring round a dead king's mound ... told by Jordanes of the burial of Attila". In Jordanes the horsemen circle the place where the body lies (laid out, before burial), not a mound; and "also told" implied a source. · Rewritten as a hedged parallel: horsemen riding round the place where a dead king lay, reciting his deeds in song (Attila, sixth-century Jordanes); "a parallel, not a source: nothing in the text says the poet knew it". Kept (true and hedged) rather than struck.
23. 3173 · l · low · "judged it" for two objects (`eorlscipe ond ellenweorc`). · "judged them".
24. 3173 · n · low · note "love him in his hearts" vs l "in spirits". · "in spirits".
25. 3180 · i · medium · "the gentlest of men and the most gracious, the kindest to his people and the most eager for renown" is the familiar four-fold run of a famous modern rendering; "gracious" is not derived from `monðwǣrust` (mon + þwǣre, "gentle to men"). · Rebuilt from the grammar: "the mildest of men and the most humane, the kindest to his people and the most eager for praise"; l unchanged ("most men-gentle").
26. 3180 · n · low · "Grundtvig's transcript supplied it": the apparatus says `Gru.tr.`, which the packet does not expand as a transcript. · "Grundtvig supplied it (the apparatus cites Gru.tr.)".
27. 3180 · n · low · ", as against the Wielder who rules the next": an inference beyond the text (no Waldend in these lines). · Struck.

Findings considered and refused (pass 1)

- 3137 `behongen` "agreeing with ād": the bare form is not the strong accusative masc. ending, but a participle with no ending beside `ād` is the usual way editors read it; label left (grammar ok, hedge is the apparatus remark already in the note).
- 3137 `unwāclīcne` "understatement meaning splendid": litotes is plain from the l/i; left.
- 3143 `on beorge` "hill": drafter flags the guess and the later contrast with 3163; left.
- 3144 `swioðole` / `lēg` / `windblond` glosses: all already flagged as guesses; Tho. "Swedish pine" and Grimm's `[ne] gelæg` correctly attributed; left.
- 3144 `lēg` masculine so `hē` is the flame: kept (lēg is masculine; glossary lēg entry agrees).
- 3150 `bundenheorde` "bound-haired": flagged guess with Grein's `heorte`; left. The Latin `anus` support for `geōmēowle` and the italic o / `sælðe` / `wonn` facts all check against the apparatus.
- 3155 `rēce`: called accusative sg. of masculine `rēc`; the -e ending is not what a plain masc. a-stem accusative shows. I could not settle this from the public-domain aids to hand, so I did not change the note or the gloss; recorded here for the orchestrator (the translation, "swallowed the smoke", is not in doubt).
- 3156 `bronda lāfe` as "remains of the pyre", `betimbredon` "built", `hliðe` supplied h: all attributed to the apparatus correctly; left.
- 3163 `nīðhēdịge` "hate-minded": hedged guess, left. i "taken out of the hoard" for `on horde ... genumen` accepted as the natural reading of `on horde`.
- 3166 `grēote` "gravel" in l and "dust" in i: the glossary senses are gravel, grit, dust, earth; left.
- 3166 "the curse ... is not mentioned again": true for 3166-3182; left.
- 3173 `duguðum dēmdon`: unresolved crux, drafter's guess is flagged in the note and the glossary; l/i differ in wording but agree in sense; left.
- 3173 closing sentence ("above all when death comes ..."): paraphrase of `þonne hē forð scile`, not a new claim; left.
- 3180 "poem's last sentence", Scyld's funeral at the start: true (Klaeber 26 ff.); left.
- Standing rendering checks: Gēata lēode, Wedra lēode, hlāford, mondryhten, winedryhten, bānhūs, heorðgenēatas, hildebord, byrne, siglu/sigle, bēna all agree with published parts.

## Pass 2 — units.json re-read after fixes

1. 3137 · n · low · Closing sentence "The arms burned with a lord are the gear of a warrior chief." is an unsupported atmospheric closer (conventions: no vague atmospheric closers). · Struck.
2. 3156 · n · low · "The remains of the pyre are the ashes and bones" stated as fact. · "presumably".

Refused in pass 2: no change to the new 3150 sentences (checked against apparatus: Bugge 3151a-55a, E. Sc. geō, Zupitza (w)igendes, MS sælðe/wonn/hyðo); no change to 3163 (genitive hyrsta now agrees with gloss); `t`, `ln`, `v` verified identical to the drafter's file (14 units); no backticks in any `n`; dots/italics in notes verified against the packet's italic list (swioðole o, lēg g, (s)īo o, sǣde d, worn r, twelfe e, līchaman ī, all explained).

## Gloss — gloss.json (every parse checked against its line)

1. nīðhēdịge · medium · "the dot marks a doubtful letter" contradicts the unit note and Klaeber's sign (vowel does not count in the metre). · Corrected.
2. hliðe · medium · "slope, hillside, headland": headland comes only from the editors' `hliðe[s nōsan]`, not from hlið. · "slope, hillside".
3. giōmorgyd · low · "feminine" (gyd is neuter, as in the entry for wordgyd). · "neuter".
4. giōmorgyd · low · "the first element is a guess": giōmor "sad" is secure; what varies is one word or two (Wy., Cha. print two). · Now "some editors print it as two words".
5. swioðole · low · gender "masculine" given for a hapax. · Gender dropped.
6. care · low · "the ending is partly supplied": the whole word is in round brackets (usual reading ceare). · Corrected.
7. wyruldcyninga · low · "wyrold" for the base word. · "wyruld".
8. dagum · low · "within ten days" vs "in ten days" in l/i/note. · "in ten days".
9. forlēton · low · "here followed by": entries must not say "here". · "followed by".
10. duguðum · low · "the sense here is a guess": same rule. · "the sense is a guess".
11. eahtodan · low · "related to eahta 'consideration'": eahta is "eight" to a reader and I could not confirm the relation from the public-domain aids. · Relation dropped.

Checked and left: all `__broaden__` entries begin with the old entry whole plus " · " (verified by script against known-forms.json); gloss keys equal novel-forms.json exactly; geōmēowle, bundenheorde, windblond, swioðole, nīðhēdig, duguðum flagged as guesses; hyrsta genitive, bēg, hȳnðu, egesan consistent with the notes; hlāfordes "from hlāf-weard 'loaf-ward'" matches the existing hlāford entry; verb classes and cases checked against the lines (behōn VII, hēofan II, swōgan, gebrecan IV, geniman IV, gelicgan V, ondrǣdan VII, frēogan/herian weak II, secgan III, sculan subjunctive, lǣded passive with weorðan).

Open item for the orchestrator (not a defect fixed here): 3182 `lofgeornost` is a famous crux with no house rendering; the drafter's choice ("most praise-eager" / "eager for praise", flagged as a guess) should go into QUESTIONS.md. Also the 3155 `rēce` ending question above.
